summary:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive "play-and-learn" web game built for the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. Space education often oversimplifies real engineering trade-offs or makes them too technical for young learners. Our game bridges that gap by letting students step into the role of a junior astronaut managing space mission operations.
Through hands-on gameplay, players make real-time decisions to balance critical mission demands—such as life support, power management, radiation safety, and resource allocation—experiencing firsthand how engineering choices determine mission success. Grounded in official NASA STEM Engagement and Moon to Mars mission concepts, the platform turns complex spaceflight science into intuitive, rewarding challenges.
By combining playful exploration with authentic space mission rules, Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer builds foundational STEM skills and inspires young learners to think like real NASA engineers.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive "play-and-learn" web game built for the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge. Players step into the role of a rookie astronaut and complete guided training missions designed around real space exploration concepts. Through interactive tasks, decision-making challenges, and knowledge checks, users learn how astronauts prepare for launch, operate in space environments, and balance critical mission requirements such as life support, power management, and crew safety.

Benefits & Intended Impact
Traditional space science resources can feel overly complex or passive for younger audiences. By turning astronaut preparation into an approachable, browser-based game, our project makes STEM learning active, enjoyable, and accessible to students of all backgrounds. Our intended impact is to spark early curiosity in space science, strengthen problem-solving skills, and inspire the next generation of engineers, scientists, and explorers to see themselves as part of NASA's Moon to Mars journey.

Tools, Software & Technologies Used
We built and deployed Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer as a responsive web application using the Emergent development platform along with modern web technologies (HTML, CSS, and JavaScript/React) so players can launch and play the game directly in any standard web browser without needing special hardware or downloads. To keep the missions scientifically grounded, we referenced official NASA STEM Engagement and Artemis educational resources.

Creativity & Design Factors Considered
Rather than presenting space facts as a static textbook or simple quiz, we designed the experience around active play and immediate feedback so learners understand why astronaut decisions matter. When building the game, our team prioritized three key factors:

  • Accessibility & Ease of Use: A clean, intuitive interface with simple controls tailored for school-age learners and beginners.
  • Balance of Fun & Accuracy: Gamified rewards and mission progression paired with authentic NASA spaceflight concepts.
  • Zero-Barrier Access: Hosting the trainer online as a lightweight web app so classrooms, families, and students anywhere can play instantly.
